failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial. The docs did well on the key hazards for this task: the Tag Processor overview explicitly says to use it for flat attribute edits and byte-preserving output; the template-building section directly explains filling a literal template with untrusted values, preserving attribute order by including empty attributes, and replacing placeholder text because empty elements have no #text node; set_attribute() and set_modifiable_text() both state that callers should pass plain unescaped strings and let the API encode them; get_updated_html() is clearly identified as the way to retrieve queued edits. Near-misses: the candidates copied the template pattern without checking set_modifiable_text()'s boolean return, even though the method docs say to check it. This was safe here because they first matched #text in a known template, but examples could make that precondition clearer. The docs also contain enough encoding guidance, but an explicit compact example covering quotes and angle brackets in both attributes and text would further reduce the temptation to pre-escape with htmlspecialchars().

doc_gaps.location: html-tag-processor.md, Building markup from a template / set_modifiable_text() examples
doc_gaps.problem: Examples call set_modifiable_text() after matching #text but do not check the returned bool, while the method contract says to always check the return value. This can teach silent no-op handling when a placeholder is missing or the current token is not modifiable.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Update examples to either guard the return value or explicitly state that the known #text placeholder is a required precondition. Prefer showing a small fail-closed pattern for template builders.

doc_gaps.location: html-tag-processor.md, set_attribute() and set_modifiable_text() encoding sections
doc_gaps.problem: The docs state that plain unescaped strings are encoded, and show ampersand examples, but they do not show a compact case with quotes and angle brackets. Those are common points where users may incorrectly pre-escape input.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general encoding example table showing that plain values containing &, quotes, <, and > should be passed directly, and that pre-escaped input will be encoded again.
